archetype.name: Play-In Team (Curry-dependent)
archetype.definition: A roughly .500 team with a break-even point margin, a mid-pack offense and defense, and a ceiling set almost entirely by whether its one star is on the floor.

report.headline: A .500 team with Curry, a lottery offense without him
report.take:
Golden State at 9-8 is almost exactly the team it was last season. Its Net Rtg of -0.8 sits 18th. Last year's 37-45 team finished at -0.6. The offense ranks 18th and the defense 15th, the same middling profile it carried a year ago. The record runs one game ahead of the margin (W vs Pt Diff +1, eight wins by differential), and the 88-87 escape against Boston is a reminder of how thin that edge is. The full-season pace of 43 wins on a negative differential describes a play-in team, not a contender.

The season has been shaped by Stephen Curry's availability. He has played 10 of 17 games, and in those he has been the best player in the building: 71.9 TS % on a 34 USG %, a 13.8 BPM, and a +22.7 On-Off. He is now listed Out. The last five games show the cost. The Warriors went 1-4 and scored 91.8 a game, 19.44 below their season average. They lost by 38 at San Antonio and by 21 to New Orleans, a team they had beaten 138-87 a week earlier. The defense barely moved over that stretch, allowing 113.4 a game, close to its season norm. This was an offensive collapse, not a general one.

The numbers also show a structural flaw that is there with or without Curry: the frontcourt. It grades F. The defense does well at keeping opponents out of the paint (Opp Rim Rate 4th), but when they get there they finish at 68.3%, 23rd. The DRB % of 70.5 is also 23rd, so second chances leak. Al Horford is shooting 42.6 TS % and Georges Niang's -4.7 BPM ranks him 80th of 86 at his position, yet both play more than Charles Bassey. Bassey has the group's best numbers (72.2 TS %, 1.8 BPM, 23rd of 92 centers). Opposing small forwards have also feasted: the Warriors allow them more over their usual output than any defense in the league. Turnovers (TOV % 25th) cost a 3-heavy offense possessions it can't spare.

The direction depends on Curry's return date, which the sheet doesn't give. With him, this offense lives up to its 3-point volume (3PA Rate 5th, 3P % 10th) and the team plays like a top-half side. Without him, Yaxel Lendeborg carries a 26.8 USG % on 56.7 TS %, and the team has been badly outscored with him on the floor. That makes for a bottom-ten offense. Expect something close to last season: hovering near .500 and fighting for a play-in spot.

strengths.title: Curry is still an elite engine
strengths.body: In his 10 games Curry has posted a 71.9 TS % on a 34 USG % with a +22.7 On-Off, and he ranks 3rd of 85 point guards. Nobody else on the roster creates efficient offense at volume. The offense's whole identity runs through him, so this strength is real but only exists when he is healthy.

strengths.title: Volume threes and second chances
strengths.body: Golden State takes a larger share of its shots from three than all but four teams and makes them at an above-league clip (36.1% against a 35.4 league average). Its ORB % of 30.3 ranks 4th, so misses often get another try. The shooting mix is a Kerr-era constant across every season in the history block. The offensive rebounding is new and worth watching against weak defensive-rebounding opponents.

strengths.title: Keeping opponents off the rim
strengths.body: Only three defenses allow a smaller share of shots at the rim (Opp Rim Rate 25.3, 4.3 below the league). Opposing centers have scored well under their norms against them. This scheme-driven positioning keeps a thin frontcourt from being exposed even more. It is why the defense rates as average rather than bad.

concerns.title: The offense without Curry
concerns.body: The last five games produced 91.8 points a game, a drop of 19.44 from the season average, and a -21.6 margin. The defense held near its norm, so the slide is about shot creation. With Curry Out and no return date in the sheet, this is the single biggest drag on the outlook.

concerns.title: An F frontcourt that can't finish possessions
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 68.3% at the rim (23rd), and the Warriors rank 23rd in DRB %. The group's minutes skew toward Niang and Horford, who are struggling, while Bassey, the most productive big, plays the fewest minutes. Shifting minutes to Bassey is the obvious internal fix. Unless that happens, the defensive glass will keep costing possessions.

concerns.title: Small forwards and turnovers
concerns.body: Opposing small forwards score 2.88 points over their usual output, the worst mark in the league. Their combined points, rebounds and assists over expectation also rank last. Lendeborg's -36.8 On-Off in the most minutes on the team is a related red flag, though early and noisy. Add a TOV % of 14.7 (25th), and the margin for error is small.

trend.note: An eight-game winning streak was followed by a five-game losing streak. The losing streak was the ugliest stretch of the season, and the scoring drop from October's 116.67 to November's 108.27 points toward Curry's absence. A one-point win over Boston stopped the slide but didn't fix it.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft home games bracket a real test in Portland
weekAhead.body:
Two of the three games are at home against the league's bottom tier. Sacramento is 2-14, last on the site, with a 119.7 DRtg (27th) and the worst opponent rim finishing in the league. The Clippers are 4-11 with a 25th-ranked defense and the fewest rebounds per game. Even a Curry-less offense should find points against both, and a 2-1 week is the reasonable target.

The Portland road game is the opposite. The Blazers are 10-6, 7th on the site, top-eight on both ends, and they hold small forwards to fewer points than any defense in the league. That takes away a wing-heavy creation plan. Losing there is expected. Losing either home game would say the recent slide is more than a bad week.

keyMatchups.title: Bassey against Portland's soft middle
keyMatchups.body: Portland smothers wings but gives centers more over their norms than any defense in the league. That suits Bassey's 72.2 TS % rim finishing. Feeding the big rather than forcing it through Lendeborg is the Warriors' best path to an upset on the road.

keyMatchups.title: Offensive glass against the Clippers
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers rank last in rebounds per game and 20th in DRB %. Golden State's 4th-ranked ORB % should create extra possessions. That matters because the Clippers shoot 38.7% from three (2nd), so the Warriors need volume to offset that efficiency.

keyMatchups.title: Sacramento's broken defense
keyMatchups.body: Sacramento's 119.7 DRtg ranks 27th and its 56.6 Opp eFG % ranks 29th. If the Warriors' offense can't get well here, at home, the problem runs deeper than one missing star.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the scoring rebounds from 91.8 a game against Sacramento and the Clippers, and whether Bassey's minutes climb.

restOfSeason.body:
This roster's baseline is last season's: a team with a slightly negative margin that takes and makes plenty of threes, defends the paint by position rather than size, and leaks on the defensive glass. The +1 W vs Pt Diff is small and will likely wash out, so the record should drift toward the margin rather than away from it. The recent five-game collapse is not the baseline either. It is a Curry-less snapshot, and his 10 healthy games show a team that outscores people.

The central estimate is a finish in the high 30s to low 40s, roughly where the 43-win pace sits, with the low end if Curry's absence stretches long. The upside needs a healthy Curry plus a frontcourt rotation that leans on Bassey. A finish somewhere in the 38-44 range points to the play-in, with outright playoff seeding unlikely in a division where the Lakers are already 14-3.

confidence.note: 17 games; the profile matches last season, but Curry's return date is unknown.
